- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion.  
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; apply downward bias of 2–4% for first 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows strong downward trend + low sentiment, model often fails to recognize continuation; extend downward bias by 1–3% beyond trend.  
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive abruptly, model lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment change.
